Components / Media

Photo pile

.dr-stack · .dr-stack__shot · components/media.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

  1. 1.dr-stackThe vertical stack the pile is built on; with shots inside it takes 8 / 4 padding and keeps its 8px gap.
  2. 2.dr-stack__shot:nth-child(1)The first frame: right-aligned, tilted 3deg, at the back (z-index 1).
  3. 3.dr-stack__shot:nth-child(2)The second: left-aligned, −3.5deg, pulled up by −14% of the column's width (z-index 2).
  4. 4.dr-stack__shot:nth-child(3)The third: right-aligned with a 6% inset, 2deg, on top (z-index 3). The later frame sits on top, so the pile reads front-to-back downward.
  5. 5imgThe photograph: cover inside a 62%-wide 3 / 2 frame with a 3px --text-on-night edge (the page cream, --cream-50), the 13 media radius and a --bg-well ground while it loads. A border, never a shadow.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: (.dr-stack__shot).

States

No state of its own: the photographs are read, and nothing in the pile takes focus.

When to use

Several photographs from one order, shown the way a phone shows several photographs: a loose pile, not a grid. One screen carries it, delivery-aerial, where the client's deliverable is a set rather than a single file. The alternating tilt is the whole trick: one shared angle reads as a skewed grid, opposed angles read as a pile somebody set down. No green anywhere near it; the pile is photographs and page ground.

Every frame keeps its own descriptive alt, numbered n of 3, because a partly covered photograph still carries meaning (WCAG 1.1.1). The tilt is static, with no transition and no animation, so reduced motion has nothing to switch off (WCAG 2.3.3). No text is rotated. The photographs are not re-cropped: the masters are all 1.500, so 3 / 2 is the shoot's own ratio.

One departure is recorded and left as built: the reference covers 35% and the build 28.1%, because .dr-stack's 8px gap pushes back against the overlap. gap: 0 would land 33.9%.

Sources: DESIGN.md § The photo pile · kit.html Photo pile · § Imagery

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Three delivery photos of one aerial order on the page ground, each with a numbered alt.

Don’t

A pile of one. A single tilted photograph is not a set, it is a crooked picture. One delivery photo takes the media well as a photograph, or a cover card when it carries a file line.
